blocks.content: The Commission shall have all the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

rows: Supervisory and advisory body for vigilance matters and corruption prevention
Premier investigating agency for economic offences, corruption, and complex crimes
Statutory body under the CVC Act, 2003
Non-statutory body deriving powers from the DSPE Act, 1946
Powers of a Civil Court (summoning, requiring documents)
Powers of Police Officers (search, seizure, arrest, filing charge-sheets)

items: CVC has no direct powers to investigate state government employees; its jurisdiction is strictly confined to Central Government officials and specified public sector entities.
CVC's powers over the CBI are limited to superintendence regarding corruption cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act, not general criminal investigations.
While CVC possesses civil court powers to summon witnesses and compel document production, it functions primarily as an advisory and supervisory body without independent prosecution sanction power.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The CVC exercises superintendence over the functioning of the Delhi Special Police Establishment (CBI) regarding offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
While conducting an inquiry, the CVC has all the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
The Central Government and its agencies are required to consult the CVC on making rules and regulations governing vigilance matters of Central Services.
The Commission tenders advice to the Central Government, corporations established under Central Acts, and government companies on vigilance matters.
The CVC presents an annual report on its performance to the President of India, who causes it to be laid before each House of Parliament.
